Home/Private dining

Private dining

Your people.
A table of your own.

A birthday supper, a family gathering, or a reason to bring everyone together. Start with the occasion, then shape an evening around it.

Ask about a gathering
01

An occasion, at your pace.

Good gatherings need room for conversation. A shared menu keeps the table connected, with time to arrive, settle in, and enjoy each course. Tell us what matters to your group so the food and the flow can fit the evening.

02

A few details make a difference.

Before planning a group meal, it helps to understand the size of the party, the preferred date, and any dietary needs. Seating, menu choices, availability, and costs would be confirmed with the restaurant.

  • Your preferred date and approximate group size
  • The occasion and the atmosphere you have in mind
  • Dietary requirements to discuss before choosing the menu
03

Make the table your starting point.

Browse the seasonal menu for a feel for the kitchen. Group arrangements may differ from individual dining, so a request is the beginning of the conversation rather than a confirmed reservation.

Can a group choose a shared menu?

That is the idea behind this concept. In a real restaurant, the dishes, dietary requirements, serving style, and price would be agreed before the event.
